question: How do I reset my password if I forget it?
answer: On the sign-in screen choose Forgot password, enter your e-mail, answer the security question you picked when you registered, and set a new password. The new password needs at least 8 characters with at least one letter and one digit. A successful reset also clears failed attempts and unlocks a temporarily locked account.
keywords: forgot password, reset password, change password, security question, cannot sign in

question: Why is my account locked after wrong password attempts?
answer: The sign-in uses progressive lockout: the 3rd wrong password locks the account for 5 minutes, the 4th for 15 minutes, and the 5th locks it permanently. A permanently locked account can only be opened by an Admin (Admin → Users & access → Unlock account), or by resetting the password with your security question.
keywords: account locked, lockout, too many attempts, wrong password, unlock account

question: What can each user role access in FranchiseOps AI?
answer: There are five roles. 1) Admin: every page, including Admin and the Data Feed Center. 2) Franchise Owner: all operational pages plus the Data Feed Center (not Admin); can approve actions. 3) Store Manager: Copilot, Approvals, Workforce, Outlets, Inventory, Sentiment, Audit, Reports, Notifications, Digital Twin, Command Center, scoped to their own outlet. 4) Staff: Copilot, Approvals (view), Notifications, Command Center, scoped to their outlet. 5) Customer: Copilot, Sentiment and Profile. Opening a page or action a role does not have returns 403 (access denied).
keywords: roles, permissions, rbac, access rights, who can see, privileges, 403

question: How do I add a new user or invite a team member?
answer: Admin → Users & access → Invite: enter the new user's e-mail, a user name and the role. The app creates the account with a temporary password and e-mails it; the user signs in and changes it under My Profile. Self-service sign-up only ever creates Customer or Staff accounts, so higher roles must be given by an Admin.
keywords: invite user, add user, create account, new employee login, onboard user

question: How do I change a user's role?
answer: Admin → Users & access → choose the user and the new role → Save. The role is re-read on every request, so the change applies immediately without the user signing out. Every change is written to the audit log.
keywords: change role, promote user, make admin, update permissions, assign role

question: How do I restrict a store manager to only one outlet?
answer: Admin → Users & access → Outlet scope: pick the Store Manager or Staff account and the outlet. Scoped users then see only that outlet's rows, tickets and actions in every page and in the Copilot.
keywords: outlet scope, assign outlet, limit access, one store, scoped user

question: How do I deactivate an employee's login when they leave?
answer: Admin → Users & access → Deactivate/Reactivate: pick the account and choose Deactivate. The user can no longer sign in and existing sessions stop working; history and audit records are kept. Reactivate restores access.
keywords: deactivate user, disable login, remove access, employee left, offboarding

question: Which PDF reports can I download from the Reports page?
answer: Reports → PDF reports offers: Executive franchise report, Outlet performance report (one outlet), Inventory report, Workforce report, Marketing report, Audit & compliance report and the Franchise action plan. The Data exports (CSV) tab gives raw tables. Reports are available to Admin, Franchise Owner and Store Manager (a Store Manager only sees their own outlet).
keywords: download report, pdf report, export report, executive report, print report

question: How do I upload sales or stock data from a CSV or Excel file?
answer: Open Data Feed Center → Upload, choose the target table (for example sales) and upload a CSV or XLSX. Columns are auto-mapped, every row is validated, good rows are upserted into the live tables and bad rows are quarantined with a reason under Quality & rejects. Other options: Live API push (POST JSON with the X-API-Key header), URL feeds and a folder inbox. Only Admin and Franchise Owner can use the Data Feed Center.
keywords: upload data, import csv, excel upload, data feed, load sales file, pos data

question: What is the Digital Twin and does it change live data?
answer: The Digital Twin is a what-if lab. It runs the same agents and models on a private copy of the database, so it never changes live data. You can stack several shocks at once (for example a demand drop plus wage inflation), see the money impact, save a scenario and compare two saved scenarios on today's data.
keywords: digital twin, what if, scenario, simulation copy, scenario lab

question: How does the approval process work for agent actions?
answer: Agents raise tickets and propose actions. Read-only checks and internal notes run automatically; anything that spends money or contacts customers (purchase orders, discounts, messages) waits on the Approvals page. Admin and Franchise Owner can approve or reject; Store Managers can view and resolve tickets for their outlet. Every approval and rejection is written to the audit log with the person and the time (IST).
keywords: approvals, approve action, reject action, pending approval, sign off

question: How do I add my own document to the Copilot's knowledge base?
answer: AI Copilot → Knowledge base → Add a document: upload a PDF or text file. It is chunked, indexed for keyword search (BM25) and embedded for meaning search, and is private to you. To add many sources for everyone, collect them with the RAG builder notebook and import the kb_export.json under Import a corpus.
keywords: upload document, knowledge base, add pdf, rag, add source

question: How does the Copilot make sure its numbers are correct?
answer: Every number comes from a read-only SQL query on the live tables, and you can ask "show the SQL" to see it. Policy and topic answers come from the knowledge base with numbered sources [1] [2]. The language model only phrases evidence; if it uses a number that is not in the evidence the answer is replaced. When nothing supports an answer the Copilot says it does not know instead of guessing.
keywords: accuracy, hallucination, trust copilot, numbers correct, sql answer, sources

question: Which languages does the Copilot understand?
answer: The Copilot translates with Facebook NLLB-200 and supports 35 languages, including English, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Bengali, Gujarati and Punjabi. Ask in your language; the answer is translated back. The Document translator tab translates text or a PDF.
keywords: languages, hindi, tamil, translate, multilingual, regional language

question: What do the red, amber and green colours on outlet health mean?
answer: Outlet health is a 0–100 score. Red means below 60 (critical: the owner reviews it weekly), amber means 60 to 79 (warning) and green/teal means 80 or above (healthy).
keywords: health colour, red amber green, outlet colour, health score band, traffic light

question: Which FSSAI licence does a restaurant outlet need?
answer: It depends on annual turnover. From 1 April 2026 the limits are: 1) Basic registration up to ₹1.5 crore (Form A); 2) State licence above ₹1.5 crore up to ₹50 crore (Form B); 3) Central licence above ₹50 crore. The old limits were ₹12 lakh and ₹20 crore. Each premises needs its own registration or licence, and it must be displayed at the outlet.
keywords: fssai licence type, basic registration, state licence, central licence, food licence turnover

question: How many Food Safety Supervisors does an outlet need under FoSTaC?
answer: FSSAI requires every food business with a State or Central licence to have at least one trained and certified Food Safety Supervisor (FoSTaC) for every 25 food handlers or part of 25, on each premises. Example: 1–25 handlers = 1 supervisor, 26–50 = 2. The supervisor trains the other food handlers on site and keeps the training records for inspections.
keywords: fostac, food safety supervisor, fss, trained supervisor, food handler training

question: What is the temperature danger zone for food?
answer: The danger zone is 5°C to 60°C, where bacteria multiply fastest. Keep cold food at 5°C or below, hot food at 60°C or above, and limit the time high-risk food spends in between (no more than 2 hours at room temperature).
keywords: danger zone, unsafe temperature, bacteria growth, temperature range

question: At what temperature should hot food be held for service?
answer: FSSAI Schedule 4 sets hot holding at 60°C or above. The FSSAI hygiene-rating audit checklist uses a stricter 65°C for vegetarian and 70°C for non-vegetarian food, so holding at 65°C or more (70°C for non-veg) is the safe target. Check with a probe thermometer and log it.
keywords: hot holding, bain marie temperature, keep food hot, serving temperature

question: How should cooked food be cooled before refrigeration?
answer: Cool cooked food from 60°C to 21°C within 2 hours, or to 5°C within 4 hours, then refrigerate it at 5°C or below. Use shallow containers, an ice bath or a blast chiller; do not leave it standing at room temperature to cool.
keywords: cooling food, chill cooked food, blast chiller, cooling rule

question: What is the correct way to reheat food?
answer: Reheated food must reach a core temperature of at least 74°C (FSSAI Schedule 4) and is then held at 60°C or more. Reheat on a direct heat source; never reheat in a bain-marie, under a heat lamp or by adding hot water. Food that was reheated and not used is discarded, not reheated again.
keywords: reheat, reheating temperature, leftover food, core temperature

question: What are the seven principles of HACCP?
answer: 1) Conduct a hazard analysis. 2) Identify the critical control points (CCPs). 3) Set critical limits for each CCP. 4) Monitor each CCP. 5) Set corrective actions for when a limit is missed. 6) Verify that the system works. 7) Keep records and documentation.
keywords: haccp, haccp principles, critical control point, food safety plan

question: What is the difference between FIFO and FEFO?
answer: FIFO (First In, First Out) uses the oldest received stock first. FEFO (First Expired, First Out) uses the stock with the earliest expiry date first, even if it arrived later. For perishables FEFO is safer because delivery date and expiry date do not always follow the same order.
keywords: fifo, fefo, stock rotation, first in first out, first expired

question: Do food handlers need a medical fitness certificate?
answer: Yes. Under FSSAI Schedule 4 food handlers must be medically examined by a registered medical practitioner at least once a year and the fitness certificates kept on file for inspection. Anyone with diarrhoea, vomiting, fever, infected wounds or a skin infection must not handle food until cleared.
keywords: medical certificate, medical fitness, health check food handler, annual medical

question: What records should an outlet keep for a food safety inspection?
answer: Keep: 1) the FSSAI licence and FoSTaC certificates; 2) temperature logs for fridges, freezers, hot holding and cooking; 3) cleaning and sanitation schedules; 4) pest control service records; 5) food handler medical certificates and training records; 6) supplier and goods-receiving records; 7) water test reports; 8) corrective actions from past audits.
keywords: inspection records, documents for audit, food safety records, logs to keep

question: How should allergens be managed in the kitchen?
answer: 1) Keep an allergen matrix for every menu item (for example milk, egg, peanut, tree nuts, wheat/gluten, soy, fish, shellfish, sesame, mustard). 2) Train staff to answer allergen questions and never guess. 3) Store allergen ingredients separately and labelled. 4) Use separate or freshly cleaned utensils and boards for allergen-free orders. 5) Re-check the matrix whenever a recipe or supplier changes.
keywords: allergy, allergen, nut allergy, gluten, food allergy customer

question: What should staff do if they see a pest in the kitchen?
answer: 1) Stop food preparation in the affected area and protect or discard exposed food. 2) Inform the shift lead and Store Manager immediately; pest evidence is a critical violation that closes the affected station. 3) Call the pest-control contractor. 4) Clean and sanitise the area. 5) Record the incident and the corrective action for the next audit.
keywords: pest, cockroach, rodent, rat, pest sighting, infestation

question: What is the GST rate on restaurant food?
answer: Restaurant services (dine-in, takeaway and delivery) are taxed at 5% GST without input tax credit (2.5% CGST + 2.5% SGST). Only restaurants in 'specified premises' (hotels with a room tariff above ₹7,500 a night) charge 18% with input tax credit. GST 2.0 (from 22 September 2025) did not change the restaurant rate.
keywords: gst rate, gst on food, restaurant tax, 5 percent gst, itc restaurant

question: When does a franchise outlet need GST registration?
answer: A restaurant supplies a service, so registration is compulsory once aggregate turnover crosses ₹20 lakh in a year (₹10 lakh in special category states). An outlet that sells through Swiggy or Zomato normally needs a GSTIN anyway to be listed.
keywords: gst registration, gstin, gst threshold, turnover limit gst

question: What is the GST composition scheme for restaurants?
answer: Restaurants with turnover up to ₹1.5 crore in the previous year can opt for composition and pay a flat 5% of turnover. They cannot claim input tax credit, cannot collect GST from customers on the bill, cannot make inter-state supplies, and must display 'composition taxable person' at the outlet. It is simpler but restricts selling through delivery platforms.
keywords: composition scheme, composition dealer, small restaurant gst, flat gst

question: Who pays GST on Swiggy and Zomato orders?
answer: Since 1 January 2022, under Section 9(5) of the CGST Act, the delivery platform collects the 5% GST from the customer and pays it to the government. The restaurant does not charge or deposit GST again on those orders, but must report them in its returns.
keywords: swiggy, zomato, delivery app gst, section 9(5), aggregator gst

question: Is GST charged on franchise fees and royalty?
answer: Yes. Franchise fees and royalty paid to the franchisor are a service and attract 18% GST, charged by the franchisor on its invoice. A franchisee paying 5% GST without ITC on restaurant sales cannot set this GST off, so it is a real cost.
keywords: gst royalty, gst franchise fee, tax on royalty

question: Can a restaurant force customers to pay a service charge?
answer: No. Under the Central Consumer Protection Authority guidelines (July 2022), restaurants cannot add a service charge to the bill automatically or by default, or collect it under another name. The Delhi High Court upheld these guidelines in March 2025. A tip is voluntary; customers can complain on the National Consumer Helpline (1915).
keywords: service charge, mandatory tip, bill service charge, consumer complaint

question: How do I calculate the food cost percentage?
answer: Food cost % = (Opening stock + Purchases − Closing stock) ÷ Food sales × 100. Example: (₹40,000 + ₹1,20,000 − ₹35,000) ÷ ₹4,50,000 = 27.8%. The network benchmark is 25–30% of food and beverage revenue.
keywords: food cost, food cost percent, cogs, cost of goods

question: What is prime cost and what should it be?
answer: Prime cost = food and beverage cost + total labour cost (salaries, overtime, benefits). It is the largest controllable cost. With food cost at 25–30% and labour at most 28% of revenue, prime cost should stay around 55–60% of sales; above about 65% profit is at risk.
keywords: prime cost, food plus labour, controllable cost

question: How do I calculate the break-even point of an outlet?
answer: Break-even sales = Fixed costs ÷ Contribution margin ratio, where contribution margin ratio = (Sales − Variable costs) ÷ Sales. Example: fixed costs ₹3,00,000 a month and variable costs 60% of sales give a 40% margin, so break-even = ₹3,00,000 ÷ 0.40 = ₹7,50,000 of sales a month.
keywords: break even, breakeven, payback, fixed cost, contribution margin

question: Do restaurants need to issue GST e-invoices?
answer: E-invoicing (IRN) applies only to B2B invoices of businesses whose aggregate turnover exceeds ₹5 crore in any year since 2017-18. Normal bills to walk-in customers (B2C) do not need an e-invoice. B2B bills (for example corporate catering) from such a business do.
keywords: e-invoice, einvoice, irn, b2b invoice

question: When is an employee eligible for gratuity?
answer: Under the Code on Social Security (in force from 21 November 2025): permanent employees after 5 years of continuous service; fixed-term employees after 1 year, paid pro rata. Gratuity = 15 days' wages for each completed year (last wage × 15 ÷ 26 × years).
keywords: gratuity, gratuity eligibility, gratuity formula, fixed term gratuity

question: What are the ESI contribution rules?
answer: Employees earning gross wages up to ₹21,000 a month (₹25,000 for persons with disability) are covered by ESI. The employee pays 0.75% and the employer 3.25% of gross wages (4% in total), deposited by the 15th of the following month.
keywords: esi, esic, employee state insurance, esi ceiling, esi rate

question: What are the PF contribution rules for staff?
answer: Employee and employer each contribute 12% of PF wages (basic + DA). From 17 September 2026 the statutory EPF wage ceiling is ₹25,000 a month (S.O. 5109(E)); it was ₹15,000 before that. Contributions are due by the 15th of the following month.
keywords: pf, epf, provident fund, pf ceiling, pf contribution

question: How much maternity leave are female employees entitled to?
answer: 26 weeks of paid maternity leave for the first two children and 12 weeks from the third child. Adopting and commissioning mothers get 12 weeks. An establishment with 50 or more employees must provide a creche.
keywords: maternity leave, pregnancy leave, maternity benefit, creche

question: What is the overtime pay rate under the new labour codes?
answer: Overtime must be paid at twice the ordinary rate of wages, and overtime needs the worker's consent. Normal working time is up to 48 hours a week; the company policy also flags overtime beyond 9 hours a week for Store Manager approval and beyond 16 hours for the Franchise Owner.
keywords: overtime pay, overtime rate, double wages, extra hours pay

question: Do we need an Internal Committee under the POSH Act?
answer: Yes. Every workplace with 10 or more employees must set up an Internal Committee to handle sexual-harassment complaints: a senior woman employee as presiding officer, at least two employee members and one external member from an NGO or legal background; at least half the members must be women. Display the policy and the committee details and file an annual report.
keywords: posh, sexual harassment, internal committee, icc, workplace harassment

question: Is an appointment letter mandatory for every employee?
answer: Yes. Under the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code (in force from 21 November 2025) every employee, including those hired before, must receive a written appointment letter stating the job, wages and social security details.
keywords: appointment letter, offer letter, employment contract, joining letter

question: How should a new employee be onboarded at an outlet?
answer: 1) Appointment letter, ID and bank details on day 1. 2) PF/ESI registration. 3) Medical fitness certificate for food handlers. 4) Food-safety induction before the first solo shift. 5) Uniform, grooming and hygiene rules. 6) Buddy shifts for the first week. 7) 30-day check-in with the manager. Structured onboarding in the first 30 days is one of the strongest drivers of retention.
keywords: onboarding, new hire, induction, joining process, first day

question: What is the difference between a franchise fee and a royalty?
answer: The franchise fee is a one-time payment for the right to open an outlet under the brand, the training and the launch support. A royalty is an ongoing payment, usually a percentage of net sales (5% of net sales, paid monthly, in this network), for continued use of the brand and support. Many networks also charge a separate marketing-fund contribution.
keywords: franchise fee, royalty, initial fee, ongoing fee

question: What is an exclusive territory in a franchise agreement?
answer: An exclusive territory is an area (for example a radius in km or a list of PIN codes) where the franchisor promises not to open or license another outlet of the same brand. The agreement should also say whether online and delivery sales into that area count, and whether the territory depends on meeting sales targets.
keywords: territory, exclusive area, protected territory, radius clause

question: Is there a franchise law in India like the US franchise disclosure document?
answer: No. India has no franchise-specific law and no mandatory disclosure document like the US FDD (FTC Franchise Rule). Franchising is governed by general law: the Indian Contract Act, the Trade Marks Act, the Competition Act, FEMA for foreign franchisors and tax laws. Franchisees should ask for financials and unit data and get the agreement reviewed by a lawyer.
keywords: franchise law india, fdd, disclosure document, franchise regulation

question: What licences are needed to open a new food outlet in India?
answer: Typically: 1) FSSAI registration or licence; 2) GST registration; 3) Shops and Establishments registration; 4) Trade or health licence from the municipal corporation; 5) Fire NOC; 6) Signage licence; 7) Eating-house licence from the police in some cities; 8) Liquor licence if alcohol is served; 9) Music (copyright) licence if music is played. Requirements vary by state and city.
keywords: licences new outlet, open restaurant licence, permits, fire noc, trade licence

question: What should be on the daily outlet opening checklist?
answer: 1) Check fridge, freezer and hot-holding temperatures and log them. 2) Check staff attendance, uniforms and health. 3) Receive and inspect deliveries (temperature, expiry, quantity). 4) Clean and sanitise prep areas. 5) Check stock of top items and the reorder list. 6) Test POS, card machine and printers. 7) Count the opening cash float. 8) Brief the shift on targets, promotions and yesterday's complaints.
keywords: opening checklist, start of day, morning checklist, store opening

question: What should be on the daily closing checklist?
answer: 1) Cash up and reconcile the POS (cash variance above 2% is investigated). 2) Submit the daily sales. 3) Record waste and stock counts of key items. 4) Store, label and date leftover food or discard it. 5) Clean equipment, floors and drains. 6) Log final fridge and freezer temperatures. 7) Switch off gas and non-essential equipment. 8) Lock up and set the alarm.
keywords: closing checklist, end of day, night closing, store closing

question: How should staff handle an angry customer complaint?
answer: Use LAST: Listen without interrupting, Apologise sincerely, Solve it (replace, remake or refund within the shift lead's limit), Thank the customer. Then record the complaint, tell the Store Manager about repeat issues, and close it within 24 hours. Never argue or blame the customer.
keywords: angry customer, complaint handling, upset customer, service recovery steps

question: What is Net Promoter Score and how is it calculated?
answer: NPS asks 'How likely are you to recommend us to a friend?' on a 0–10 scale. Promoters answer 9–10, passives 7–8, detractors 0–6. NPS = % promoters − % detractors, giving a range of −100 to +100. The network target is 45 or more against an industry average of 32.
keywords: nps, net promoter score, recommend score, promoters detractors

question: What is inventory turnover and how is it calculated?
answer: Inventory turnover = Cost of goods sold ÷ Average inventory value, for the same period. Days of inventory = 365 ÷ turnover. Higher turnover means fresher stock and less cash tied up; for perishables in food service, stock usually turns weekly or faster.
keywords: inventory turnover, stock turnover, stock turns, days of inventory

question: What is economic order quantity and how is it calculated?
answer: Economic order quantity (EOQ) is the order size that minimises total ordering plus holding cost: EOQ = √(2 × D × S ÷ H), where D = annual demand in units, S = cost per order and H = holding cost per unit per year. Example: D = 12,000, S = ₹500, H = ₹20 gives EOQ = √600,000 ≈ 775 units.
keywords: eoq, economic order quantity, order size, how much to order

question: What is ABC analysis in inventory management?
answer: ABC analysis ranks items by annual consumption value. A items are about 20% of items but about 70–80% of value: count them often and control tightly. B items are the middle. C items are many low-value items with simple controls. It tells managers where to spend counting and ordering effort.
keywords: abc analysis, inventory classification, pareto inventory

question: What is inventory shrinkage and how can it be reduced?
answer: Shrinkage is stock that is paid for but not sold: spoilage, over-portioning, theft, wrong receiving and recording errors. Reduce it with FEFO rotation, standard recipes and portion tools, checking every delivery against the invoice, daily counts of high-value items, a waste log, CCTV on stores, and comparing theoretical with actual usage weekly.
keywords: shrinkage, stock loss, wastage, theft, missing stock

question: What should a store do during a power cut to keep food safe?
answer: 1) Keep fridge and freezer doors closed; a closed fridge stays cold about 4 hours and a full freezer about 48 hours. 2) Switch to the generator or inverter for refrigeration first. 3) Log temperatures every hour. 4) Discard high-risk chilled food that has been above 5°C for more than 2 hours. 5) Inform the Store Manager and record the incident.
keywords: power cut, power outage, electricity failure, generator, refrigeration failure

question: How can I see the SQL query behind a Copilot answer?
answer: After any data answer, type "show the SQL" (or "how did you calculate that") and the Copilot shows the exact read-only query it ran. The SQL is also shown under each exact answer, and the rows can be downloaded as CSV.
keywords: see sql, view query, sql behind answer, how calculated, query used

question: How should prepared food be labelled and stored in the fridge?
answer: Label every container with the item name, the preparation date and time, the use-by date and the initials of the person who made it. Store it covered at 5°C or below, ready-to-eat food above raw food, raw meat on the bottom shelf, and use it by FEFO. Discard anything unlabelled or past its use-by date.
keywords: label food, date labelling, use by label, fridge storage, storage order
